question: to the Commission Stefano Cavedagna (ECR) Subject:

The forthcoming circular economy act, due for publication in Q3 2026, is intended to make the EU a global leader in the circular economy by 2030 by establishing a fully integrated single market for secondary raw materials, increasing the supply of high-quality recycled materials, and stimulating demand for these materials within the EU. However, the 2026 Annual Single Market and Competitiveness Report highlights that, despite some progress, circularity in the EU is improving only slowly because of persistent barriers and fragmentation within the single market. It stressed that divergent national rules for waste and secondary raw materials continue to hinder the uptake of circular practices and create additional costs and barriers to cross-border trade, undermining both environmental ambition and the single market’s integrity. Given the EU’s circularity objectives and the current state of the single market for goods and waste: 1.

How will the Commission ensure that the forthcoming circular economy act effectively supports a functioning and integrated single market for secondary raw materials while accelerating progress on meeting the EU circularity targets?

Will the Commission base the upcoming act on Article 114 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union – the legal basis for establishing and ensuring the functioning of the single market – to provide a uniform regulatory framework and prevent further fragmentation?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (9.6.2026) A functioning and integrated single market for secondary raw materials is paramount to accelerate progress on meeting the EU circularity targets. Currently, the business case for circular economy is hampered by regulatory obstacles. Complex legislation, implemented differently across Member States, hinders the business case for circularity. Measures under the Circular Economy Act are being considered to ensure the regulatory framework is simplified and barriers within the Single Market are addressed1. Potential interventions may cover improving the recognition of the ‘end of waste’ status across Member States and the simplification, digitalisation and further harmonisation of extended producer responsibility schemes2. The Circular Economy Act proposal is under development, and as such, its precise legal basis has yet to be determined. The Commission is fully committed to ensuring that the Circular Economy Act establishes a well-functioning Single Market for secondary raw materials in line with broader sustainability and economic objectives. Further details on the legal framework will be provided in due course.
